description.title: Moon Geocentric Position
description.what: Computes astrometric geocentric RA/Dec of the Moon at given epochs. Accuracy reference is JPL Horizons (astrometric geocentric, ICRF, Earth geocenter, TT).
description.why: Moon position accuracy varies significantly between libraries. JPL Horizons (DE441) provides a high-accuracy external reference.
description.units: Angular separation in arcseconds between JPL Horizons reference and candidate positions.
description.interpret: Lower error = closer to JPL Horizons DE441 ephemeris. Differences measure absolute ephemeris accuracy, not cross-library agreement.
description.performance_contract: Timed scope: lunar ephemeris evaluation per epoch. Input parsing and output serialisation are outside the timed loop.

alignment.time_input: JD (Julian Date), TT scale for precession/nutation, UT1 for sidereal time
alignment.time_scales: TT for BPN matrix; UT1≈TT-69.184s simplified
alignment.leap_seconds: not applicable (JD input, no UTC conversion in this experiment)
alignment.ephemeris_source: JPL Horizons (DE441) for reference; Meeus/ELP 2000/DE440 for candidates

library_notes.astropy: The 'astropy' adapter uses public Astropy Time and SkyCoord APIs. Astropy may use ERFA internally, but this adapter no longer calls ERFA/pyerfa kernels directly.

models.jpl_horizons: JPL Horizons geometric VECTORS (DE441, ICRF, VEC_CORR=NONE, Earth geocenter, TT)
models.erfa: Simplified Meeus Ch.47 (major terms only, ~10' accuracy)
models.siderust: Simplified Meeus Ch.47 (major terms only), centralized in siderust astro module
models.astropy: Simplified Meeus Ch.47 (same algorithm as ERFA adapter)
models.libnova: ELP 2000-82B geometric (ln_get_lunar_geo_posn + J2000 obliquity rotation; no nutation/aberration)
models.anise: SPK translation MOON_J2000 → EARTH_J2000 (DE440 ephemeris, geometric state vector)

alignment.accuracy_interpretation: agreement with JPL Horizons geometric VECTORS reference (no aberration / nutation)
alignment.note: Public geometric lane — JPL VECTORS (no aberration, no light-time, no nutation). Ranked as best-available model vs JPL reference: libnova uses ELP 2000-82B geometric, ERFA/Astropy use the simplified Meeus Ch.47 fallback (ERFA's eraMoon98 path is best-available when enabled), Siderust uses its centralised Meeus implementation.
